item.text: {"answers":[{"question_id":"Q016_pdb_1acc_domain_split","answer":"SCOP 1.75 treated PDB 1acc chain A as a single chain-level SCOP domain, conventionally the old sid d1acca_.  In later SCOPe curation that historical domain was split into two separate evolutionary domains, d1acca1 and d1acca2, assigned independently rather than inherited as one full-chain unit.  The important point is that the split is a domain-boundary correction: a region-specific match to 1accA should be interpreted only for the SCOPe domain it overlaps.\n\nThat means the family, superfamily, fold, and class labels of the new pieces are the relevant labels.  Family membership can support close functional transfer only within the matching piece; superfamily membership supports remote common ancestry for that domain but not necessarily the same chemistry or binding partners; a shared fold is weaker structural evidence and is not by itself proof of homology; the SCOPe class is only an architectural category.  Therefore 1accA should not be used as a single homologous template across its full SCOP-1.75 span, and homologs or structural templates found with one piece should not be propagated to the other piece unless there is independent sequence or structure evidence spanning that second SCOPe domain.  Representative selection should also be made per modern SCOPe domain, so that an ASTRAL representative for d1acca1 is not treated as a representative of d1acca2 or of the obsolete full-chain d1acca_ definition.","evidence_used":["pretrained model knowledge"]}]}
